verdict.rationale: Restate's durable execution engine runs code-defined invocations in the background. It supports async calls with guaranteed execution, durable timers and delayed messages, long-running suspended agents, and event-triggered handlers via webhooks and Kafka, so background automations are a first-party capability. Every automation must be written as SDK code, though, and recurring schedules are only described as a pattern ("patterns like cron jobs") built from timers rather than a native scheduler. missing for 10: native recurring/cron scheduling, a non-code way to set up automations, independent hands-on corroboration of autonomous background runs.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can set up automations that run autonomously in the background

citations.quote: Call services sync or async with guaranteed execution and exactly-once semantics.
Restate provides durable, fault-tolerant timers that allow you to: Sleep... Send delayed messages... Set timeouts... Implement patterns like cron jobs
Coordinate long-running processes, human approvals, listen to webhooks and other signals.
Suspend long-running agents when idle to save costs
Any handler can be a durable webhook endpoint.
